question.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $Y$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-3,7],$ compute $P(Y>3).$
question.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $Y$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

$$
f(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a},\, & a\le y\le b, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Our random variable $Y$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-3,7],$ so it has the following probability density function:

$$
f(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{10},\, & -3\le y\le 7, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y>3) & =P(3<Y<7) \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{7}f(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{7}\frac{1}{10}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{7-3}{10} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
